note: Ps73 Asaph's crisis-of-faith (corrected; Book III opens; dense IB). The movement of a soul: near-STUMBLING from ENVY (qana) of the arrogant WICKED's ease; the wicked's inner life (PRIDE/VIOLENCE/overflowing HEARTS/SCOFF/MALICE/'How can God KNOW'); the bitter thought that keeping his heart CLEAN in INNOCENCE was vain, restraint from BETRAYing the faithful; the wrestling THOUGHT to understand - until the sanctuary, where he DISCERNED their end; the EMBITTERED, BRUTISH, IGNORANT beast-recognition; the great turn - God alone DESIRE(d), the HEART whose strength is God, the GOOD of nearness, REFUGE made, to TELL his works. God-qualifiers=7 (God's goodness, despise-the-wicked, hold/guide/counsel, portion, works). Wicked's ease/prosperity/blasphemy + their slippery-place fate + failing-flesh imagery = standalone. Every candidate roled.

dims.v: the purity the psalmist thought he kept in vain (v13)

'Truly God is good to Israel, to those who are PURE (bar) in heart' — the confessed truth the whole psalm defends against doubt; bar here purity of heart, the mark of those God is good to - the creed the psalmist clings to even as his own experience seemed to contradict it (v13)
stumble / turn aside (natah - my feet had almost stumbled)
the near-fall of faith caused by envy (v3)

'But as for me, my feet had almost STUMBLED (natah), my steps had nearly slipped' — faith on the very edge of collapse; natah here the near-fall of the believer, feet almost giving way under the scandal of the wicked's prosperity - honesty about how close he came to losing his footing
be envious / jealous (qana - I was envious of the arrogant)
seeing the prosperity of the wicked
the envy that almost made him stumble

'For I was ENVIOUS (qana) of the arrogant when I saw the prosperity of the wicked' — the root of the near-fall: envy; qana here the jealousy stirred by the ease of the godless - the corrosive resentment that a believer can feel watching the wicked flourish, the very disease the psalm diagnoses and cures
arrogant / boastful (halal - envious of the arrogant)
the same wicked whose prosperity is described (v4-12)

'I was envious of the ARROGANT (halal)' — the boastful whose success provoked the envy; halal here the arrogant, self-glorying wicked (the same root as 'praise', here perverted to self-praise) - the swaggering godless the psalmist coveted
wicked (rasha - the prosperity of the wicked)

'when I saw the prosperity of the WICKED (rasha)' — the godless whose flourishing scandalized the psalmist; rasha here the wicked at ease, whose prosperity (v4-12) and blasphemy (v11) made faith seem pointless - the problem the sanctuary resolves (v17)
pride / arrogance (gaavah - pride is their necklace)

'Therefore PRIDE (gaavah) is their necklace' — arrogance worn as a proud ornament; gaavah here the wicked's pride, so far from hidden it decks them like jewelry - self-exaltation flaunted, the inner disposition made a boast
violence (chamas - violence covers them as a garment)

'VIOLENCE (chamas) covers them as a garment' — cruelty worn like clothing; chamas here the wicked's violence, wrapping them entirely - not an occasional act but their very dress, the whole self clothed in wrong
heart (lebab - their hearts overflow with follies)
issues in scoffing and blasphemous speech (v8-9)

'their eyes swell out through fatness; their HEARTS (lebab) overflow with follies' — the inner life of the prosperous wicked, brimming with vain imaginations; lebab here their hearts so full of self-satisfied folly they spill over into scoffing and threats - prosperity feeding an overflowing, godless mind
scoff / mock (muq - they scoff and speak with malice)

'They SCOFF (muq) and speak with malice; loftily they threaten oppression' — the derision of the secure wicked; muq here the mocking of those who fear nothing, tongues set against heaven (v9) - contempt for God and man flowing from an overflowing heart

'and speak with MALICE (ra); loftily they threaten oppression' — the evil intent behind the wicked's words; ra here the malice in their speech, threatening to oppress from their height of ease - cruelty that talks, backed by power
paired with denying knowledge in the Most High

'And they say, How can God KNOW (yada)? Is there knowledge in the Most High?' — the practical atheism of the prosperous wicked; yada here the divine knowledge they deny - presuming God neither sees nor cares (cf Ps10:11, 94:7), the blasphemy their ease emboldens
keep clean / pure (zakah - I have kept my heart clean)
paired with washing his hands in innocence

'All in vain have I kept my heart CLEAN (zakah) and washed my hands in innocence' — the bitter thought that integrity was pointless; zakah here the purity the psalmist maintained, which the wicked's prosperity made seem wasted - the crisis at its sharpest: why be good if the godless flourish?
innocence (niqqayon - washed my hands in innocence)
paired with keeping the heart clean

'and washed my hands in INNOCENCE (niqqayon)' — the clean conscience the psalmist maintained; niqqayon here the innocence of hands that matched the clean heart - purity of act and heart together, which felt futile beside the wicked's untroubled ease
betray / deal faithlessly (bagad - I would have betrayed the generation of your children)
the restraint that held him back from speaking his doubt

'If I had said, I will speak thus, I would have BETRAYED (bagad) the generation of your children' — the restraint of a man who will not spread his doubt; bagad here the faithlessness to God's people he refused to commit - loving the community enough to hold his tongue while he wrestled, not scattering others' faith with his own crisis
think / consider (chashab - when I thought how to understand this)
the riddle of the wicked's prosperity
a wearisome task, until the sanctuary
resolved only when he discerned their end (v17)

'But when I THOUGHT (chashab) how to understand this, it seemed to me a wearisome task' — the exhausting mental struggle with the problem; chashab here the wrestling to make sense of the wicked's prosperity, a labor that defeated him - reason alone could not solve it, only worship could (v17)
discern / perceive (bin - then I discerned their end)
the end / destiny of the wicked
the insight that answered the wearisome thought

'until I went into the sanctuary of God; then I DISCERNED (bin) their end' — the turning-point of the psalm: worship gives what reasoning could not; bin here the sudden perception of the wicked's true destiny, gained in God's presence - the eternal perspective that dissolves the envy, seeing their prosperity is set on slippery places (v18)
be embittered / soured (chamets - when my soul was embittered)
the bitterness that made him brutish (v22)

'When my soul was EMBITTERED (chamets), when I was pricked in heart' — the soured, resentful state the psalmist looks back on; chamets (to turn sour, like leaven) here the fermenting bitterness of his crisis - a bitterness he now confesses made him brutish toward God (v22)
brutish / stupid (baar - I was brutish and ignorant)

'I was BRUTISH (baar) and ignorant; I was like a beast toward you' — the humbling self-recognition; baar here the beast-like stupidity the psalmist confesses his envy reduced him to - honest admission that his resentment was not clever but sub-human, blind before God
not know / be ignorant (yada - and ignorant)

'I was brutish and IGNORANT (yada, negated)' — the failure of understanding the psalmist owns; the not-knowing of a soul so embittered it could not see - the same knowledge the wicked deny God (v11), here the psalmist confessing his own blindness
desire / delight (chaphets - nothing on earth that I desire besides you)
whom have I in heaven but you?
held by God who guides and receives him (v23-24)

'Whom have I in heaven but you? And there is nothing on earth that I DESIRE (chaphets) besides you' — the summit of the psalm: God alone the object of desire; chaphets here the desire that has found its whole rest in God - the envy of v3 utterly cured, replaced by a longing for nothing but God himself, the most God-centred verse in the Psalter
heart (lebab - God is the strength of my heart)
though flesh and heart fail, God its strength forever
God the portion of this heart forever

'My flesh and my HEART (lebab) may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever' — the inner self anchored beyond its own failing; lebab here the heart that, though it and the body give way, is held up by God as its strength and everlasting portion (the qualifier) - faith that outlasts the body's collapse
be unfaithful / play the harlot (zanah - everyone who is unfaithful to you)
set against the psalmist's nearness to God (v28)

'you put an end to everyone who is UNFAITHFUL (zanah) to you' — the faithlessness that ends in ruin; zanah (to whore after other things) here the desertion of God by those far from him - the opposite of the psalmist, whose good is to draw near (v28), their end the ruin he once envied their prosperity
good (tob - it is good to be near God)
having made the Lord GOD his refuge
issues in making God his refuge and telling his works

'But for me it is GOOD (tob) to be near God' — the psalmist's settled conclusion, answering the opening 'God is good' (v1); tob here his own reckoning that nearness to God is the true good - not the wicked's prosperity but communion with God is what is best, the crisis fully resolved
refuge (machseh - I have made the Lord GOD my refuge)
that he may tell of God's works
issues in telling all God's works

'I have made the Lord GOD my REFUGE (machseh)' — the deliberate act of taking shelter in God; machseh here the psalmist's chosen refuge - having discerned the wicked's end and found God alone his desire, he settles his whole security in God, and lives to tell his works
tell / recount (saphar - that I may tell of all your works)
the purpose of taking refuge in God

'that I may TELL (saphar) of all your works' — the crisis resolved issuing in testimony; saphar here the recounting of God's works that crowns the psalm - the man who nearly stumbled now a witness, his restored faith become proclamation (the works being the qualifier)
good (tob - God is good to Israel)
God's goodness to the pure in heart (v1)

v1 QUALIFIER (God's goodness): 'Truly God is GOOD (tob) to Israel, to those who are pure in heart' - God's goodness is not a human IB char; the truth the psalm defends, that God is good to the pure-hearted (282360). Qualifier.
despise (bazah - you despise them as phantoms)
God despises the wicked as phantoms, the end the psalmist discerned (v20->v17)

v20 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'when you rouse yourself, you DESPISE (bazah) them as phantoms' - God's contempt for the wicked is not a human IB char; the reality the psalmist discerned (282404) - their prosperity a mere dream God dismisses on waking. Qualifier.
hold / grasp (achaz - you hold my right hand)
God holds the psalmist's hand, ground of his desire for God alone (v23->v25)

v23 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'Nevertheless, I am continually with you; you HOLD (achaz) my right hand' - God's grasping his hand is not a human IB char; the sustaining hold that keeps the psalmist whose desire is God alone (282452). Qualifier.
guide / lead (nachah - you guide me with your counsel)
God guides the psalmist with his counsel (v24->v25)

v24 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'You GUIDE (nachah) me with your counsel, and afterward you will receive me to glory' - God's guiding is not a human IB char; the leading of the one who desires God alone (282452), toward glory. Qualifier.
God's counsel by which he guides the psalmist (v24->v25)
v24 QUALIFIER (God's counsel): 'you guide me with your COUNSEL (etsah)' - God's counsel is not a human IB char; the wisdom by which he leads the one who desires him (282452). Qualifier.
portion (cheleq - God is my portion forever)
God the portion and strength of the psalmist's heart (v26)

v26 QUALIFIER (God as portion): 'God is the strength of my heart and my PORTION (cheleq) forever' - God as the psalmist's portion is not a human IB char; the everlasting inheritance that upholds his failing heart (282459) - God himself the treasure, over against the wicked's riches. Qualifier.
works (melakah - that I may tell of all your works)
God's works, which the psalmist tells (v28)
v28 QUALIFIER (God's works): 'that I may tell of all your WORKS (melakah)' - God's works are not a human IB char; the deeds the delivered psalmist recounts (282479). Qualifier.
v1: 'those who are pure in HEART (lebab)' - the heart as the seat of the purity God is good to (the char pure, 282360). Standalone (the seat of purity).
prosperity / peace (shalom - the prosperity of the wicked)

v3: 'when I saw the PROSPERITY (shalom) of the wicked' - the untroubled ease of the godless that provoked the envy; their outward flourishing (the char wicked, 282487). Standalone (the wicked's prosperity).
body / belly (ul - their bodies are fat and sleek)
v4: 'their BODIES (ul) are fat and sleek' - the healthy, well-fed frames of the wicked; their physical ease, part of the scandal of their prosperity. Standalone (the wicked's ease).
trouble / toil (amal - not in trouble as others)
v5: 'They are not in TROUBLE (amal) as others are' - the freedom from the toil and affliction that afflicts the rest; the wicked's exemption from suffering. Standalone (the wicked's ease).
cover / clothe (atah - violence covers them as a garment)
v6: 'violence COVERS (atah) them as a garment' - the enveloping of the wicked in violence (the char, 282502); the clothing-image. Standalone (the covering).
knowledge (deah - Is there knowledge in the Most High?)
v11: 'Is there KNOWLEDGE (deah) in the Most High?' - the divine knowledge the wicked deny (the char know, 282370); their blasphemous doubt. Standalone (couple to the wicked's denial).
wicked (rasha - behold, these are the wicked)

v12: 'Behold, these are the WICKED (rasha); always at ease, they increase in riches' - the summary pointing back to the wicked (the char, 282487); their perpetual ease and growing wealth. Standalone (the wicked, referring back).

v12: 'ALWAYS (olam) at ease' - the perpetual, undisturbed comfort of the wicked; the seeming permanence of their prosperity (which the sanctuary exposes as illusion, v18-20). Standalone (the wicked's ease).
riches / wealth (chayil - they increase in riches)
v12: 'they increase in RICHES (chayil)' - the growing wealth of the wicked; their prosperity, over against which God himself is the psalmist's portion (v26). Standalone (the wicked's wealth).
heart (lebab - I have kept my heart clean)
v13: 'I have kept my HEART (lebab) clean' - the heart the psalmist purified (the char clean, 282382); the seat of his maintained integrity. Standalone (the seat of the cleansing).
thus / like this (kmo - I will speak thus)

v15: 'If I had said, I will speak THUS (kmo)' - the doubting words the psalmist refrained from voicing; what he would have said, and did not (the char betrayed, 282391). Standalone (the unspoken doubt).
understand / know (yada - how to understand this)

v16: 'when I thought how to UNDERSTAND (yada) this' - the understanding the psalmist sought of the wicked's prosperity; the object of his wearisome thought (the char, 282394). Standalone (the understanding sought).
wearisome / toil (amal - it seemed a wearisome task)

v16: 'it seemed to me a WEARISOME (amal) task' - the exhausting difficulty of the problem; the toil of the psalmist's thinking (282394), which only the sanctuary relieved. Standalone (the wearisomeness).
sanctuary / holy places (miqdash - until I went into the sanctuary of God)

v17: 'until I went into the SANCTUARY (miqdash) of God' - the place of worship where the psalmist gained his insight (the char discerned, 282404); the turning-point setting. Standalone (place of the turning-point).
slippery places (chalaq - you set them in slippery places)

v18: 'Truly you set them in SLIPPERY PLACES (chalaq); you make them fall to ruin' - the precarious footing God gives the wicked; the true state of their prosperity, discerned in the sanctuary - not solid ground but a slick slope to ruin. Standalone (the wicked's fate).
be destroyed / desolate (shammah - how they are destroyed in a moment)
v19: 'How they are DESTROYED (shammah) in a moment' - the sudden ruin of the wicked; their prosperity ended in an instant, the answer to the envy. Standalone (the wicked's fate).
terrors (ballahah - swept away utterly by terrors)
v19: 'swept away utterly by TERRORS (ballahah)!' - the sudden terrors that consume the wicked; the fearful end of those who seemed so secure. Standalone (the wicked's fate).
phantoms / image (tselem - you despise them as phantoms)

v20: 'you despise them as PHANTOMS (tselem)' - the wicked as mere dream-images God dismisses on waking; the unreality of their vaunted prosperity (God's despising is the qualifier, 282423). Standalone (image of their nothingness).
heart / soul (lebab - when my soul was embittered)
v21: 'When my SOUL (lebab) was embittered' - the inner self that grew bitter; the bearer of the embittering (the char, 282427). Standalone (the embittered self).
kidneys / heart (kilyah - when I was pricked in heart)

v21: 'when I was pricked in HEART (kilyah, the inward parts)' - the inner seat where the psalmist felt the sharp pain of his bitterness; the pricking of his conscience/emotions. Standalone (the seat of the pricking).
glory / honor (kavod - afterward you will receive me to glory)

v24: 'and afterward you will receive me to GLORY (kavod)' - the glorious destiny God brings the psalmist to; the honor/glory into which he is received, the end of God's guiding (the char desire, 282452). Standalone (the glory-destination).
flesh / body (sheer - my flesh may fail)

v26: 'My FLESH (sheer) and my heart may fail' - the body that gives way; the failing frame the psalmist contrasts with God his enduring strength (the char heart, 282459). Standalone (the failing flesh).
heart (lebab - my flesh and my heart may fail)
v26: 'my flesh and my HEART (lebab) may fail' - the heart that, with the flesh, gives out; the failing inner self, over against God the strength of the heart (282459). Standalone (the failing heart).
v26: 'and my portion FOREVER (olam)' - the perpetuity of God as the psalmist's portion; the everlasting extent of the inheritance that upholds his heart (282459). Standalone (temporal).
steps / goings (ashur - my steps had nearly slipped)
v2: 'my STEPS (ashur) had nearly slipped' - the footing of the psalmist that almost gave way; the near-fall (the char stumbled, 282413). Standalone (image of near-fall).
be poured out / slip (shaphak - my steps had nearly slipped)
v2: 'my steps had nearly SLIPPED (shaphak)' - the slipping of the psalmist's feet; the near-fall of his faith (282413). Standalone (image of near-fall).
see (raah - when I saw the prosperity of the wicked)
v3: 'when I SAW (raah) the prosperity of the wicked' - the seeing that provoked the envy (the char envious, 282483); the sight that stirred the crisis. Standalone (the sight).
pangs / bonds (chartsubbah - they have no pangs until death)
v4: 'For they have no PANGS (chartsubbah) until death' - the freedom from suffering the wicked enjoy; their painless ease. Standalone (the wicked's ease).
v4: 'they have no pangs until DEATH (mavet)' - death, up to which the wicked feel no pain; part of the description of their ease. Standalone (the wicked's ease).
fat / sleek (bari - their bodies are fat and sleek)
v4: 'their bodies are fat and SLEEK (bari)' - the well-nourished health of the wicked; the sign of their comfortable ease. Standalone (the wicked's ease).
be stricken / plagued (naga - not stricken like the rest of mankind)
v5: 'they are not STRICKEN (naga) like the rest of mankind' - the wicked exempt from the blows others suffer; their immunity from affliction. Standalone (the wicked's ease).
necklace / chain (anaq - pride is their necklace)
v6: 'pride is their NECKLACE (anaq)' - the image of pride worn as jewelry (the char pride, 282500); the ornament of arrogance. Standalone (image).
garment (shith - violence covers them as a garment)
v6: 'violence covers them as a GARMENT (shith)' - the clothing-image for the wicked's enveloping violence (282502). Standalone (image).
come out / swell (yatsa - their eyes swell out through fatness)
v7: 'Their eyes SWELL OUT (yatsa) through fatness' - the bulging eyes of the well-fed wicked; the image of their gross prosperity. Standalone (image).
fatness (cheleb - their eyes swell out through fatness)
v7: 'through FATNESS (cheleb)' - the fat of the prosperous wicked; the sign of their gluttonous ease. Standalone (image).
overflow / pass over (abar - their hearts overflow with follies)
v7: 'their hearts OVERFLOW (abar) with follies' - the spilling-over of the wicked's vain imaginations (the char hearts, 282509). Standalone (the overflowing).
v7: 'their hearts overflow with FOLLIES (maskith)' - the vain imaginations that fill the wicked's hearts (282509); the content of their overflowing minds. Standalone (the follies).
speak (dabar - they scoff and speak with malice)
v8: 'they scoff and SPEAK (dabar) with malice' - the speaking of the wicked; their malicious utterance (the char malice, 282514). Standalone (the speaking).
speak / threaten (dabar - loftily they threaten oppression)
v8: 'loftily they THREATEN (dabar) oppression' - the wicked's high-handed threats; their menacing speech from a place of power. Standalone (the threatening).
v8: 'they threaten OPPRESSION (osheq)' - the extortion the wicked menace others with; the content of their threats. Standalone (the oppression threatened).
set (shith - they set their mouths against the heavens)
v9: 'They SET (shith) their mouths against the heavens' - the wicked directing their blasphemous speech at heaven; their defiance of God. Standalone (blasphemy).
mouth (peh - their mouths against the heavens)
v9: 'they set their MOUTHS (peh) against the heavens' - the organ of the wicked's blasphemy, aimed at God. Standalone (blasphemy).
go / strut (halak - their tongue struts through the earth)
v9: 'and their tongue STRUTS (halak) through the earth' - the wicked's tongue roaming boastfully over the earth; their speech dominating all. Standalone (blasphemy).
return / turn back (shub - his people turn back to them)

v10: 'Therefore his people TURN BACK (shub) to them' - God's people drawn after the wicked, seduced by their success; the harm the wicked's prosperity does to the faithful. Standalone (the seduction).
drain / find (matsa - find no fault in them)
v10: 'and FIND (matsa) no fault in them' - the people drinking in the wicked's words, finding nothing to blame; the deceptive appeal of the prosperous godless. Standalone (the seduction).
at ease / secure (shalev - always at ease)
v12: 'always at EASE (shalev)' - the undisturbed security of the wicked; their carefree prosperity. Standalone (the wicked's ease).
v12: 'they INCREASE (sagah) in riches' - the growing wealth of the wicked; the multiplying of their prosperity. Standalone (the wicked's wealth).
vain / emptiness (riq - all in vain have I kept my heart clean)

v13: 'All in VAIN (riq) have I kept my heart clean' - the futility the psalmist felt his integrity had come to; the emptiness of goodness beside the wicked's ease (the char clean, 282382). Standalone (the felt futility).
wash (rachats - washed my hands in innocence)
v13: 'and WASHED (rachats) my hands in innocence' - the washing that expressed the psalmist's innocence (the char, 282386); the act of maintaining purity. Standalone (the washing).
be stricken / plagued (naga - all the day long I have been stricken)

v14: 'For all the day long I have been STRICKEN (naga)' - the constant affliction the psalmist endured while the wicked went free; his daily suffering, the sting behind the crisis. Standalone (the psalmist's affliction).
v14: 'and REBUKED (tokechah) every morning' - the daily chastening the psalmist felt; his continual affliction, contrasted with the wicked's ease. Standalone (the psalmist's affliction).
tell / recount (saphar - I will speak thus)
v15: 'If I had said, I will SPEAK (saphar) thus' - the voicing of doubt the psalmist held back; the speaking he refrained from (the char betrayed, 282391). Standalone (the restrained speech).
set / place (shith - you set them in slippery places)
v18: 'Truly you SET (shith) them in slippery places' - God's placing of the wicked on treacherous footing; the divine act behind their coming ruin. Standalone (the wicked's fate).
fall / cast down (naphal - you make them fall to ruin)
v18: 'you make them FALL (naphal) to ruin' - the downfall God brings on the wicked; their descent from the slippery places to destruction. Standalone (the wicked's fate).
ruins / desolations (mashsuah - you make them fall to ruin)
v18: 'you make them fall to RUIN (mashsuah)' - the destruction the wicked fall into; the end of their prosperity. Standalone (the wicked's fate).
moment / instant (rega - destroyed in a moment)
v19: 'How they are destroyed in a MOMENT (rega)' - the suddenness of the wicked's ruin; the instant collapse of their long-seeming ease. Standalone (the wicked's fate).
be finished / swept away (tamam - swept away utterly)
v19: 'SWEPT AWAY (tamam) utterly by terrors' - the total sweeping-away of the wicked; their complete destruction. Standalone (the wicked's fate).
come to an end / utterly (suph - swept away utterly)
v19: 'swept away UTTERLY (suph)' - the completeness of the wicked's end; total, leaving nothing. Standalone (the wicked's fate).
dream (chalom - like a dream when one awakes)
v20: 'Like a DREAM (chalom) when one awakes' - the wicked's prosperity as unreal as a dream; the image of its vanishing on God's awaking. Standalone (image).
awake (qits - a dream when one awakes)
v20: 'like a dream when ONE AWAKES (qits)' - the moment of waking that dissolves the dream; the image of the wicked's unreality. Standalone (image).
rouse / awake (ur - when you rouse yourself)

v20: 'O Lord, when you ROUSE YOURSELF (ur)' - God's awaking to judgment, at which the wicked-phantoms vanish; the image of God's dismissive waking (his despising is the qualifier, 282423). Standalone (image).
be pricked / sharpened (shanan - when I was pricked in heart)
v21: 'when I was PRICKED (shanan) in heart' - the sharp inner pain of the psalmist's bitterness; the piercing of his embittered soul (the char, 282427). Standalone (the pricking).
cut off / put an end (tsamath - you put an end to everyone unfaithful)
v27: 'you put an END (tsamath) to everyone who is unfaithful to you' - God's cutting off of the faithless (the char unfaithful, 282467); their destruction. Standalone (the fate of the unfaithful).
nearness (qorbah - it is good to be near God)
v28: 'it is good to be NEAR (qorbah) God' - the nearness to God that is the psalmist's good (the char good, 282471); the communion he prizes above all. Standalone (the nearness sought).
set / make (shith - I have made the Lord GOD my refuge)
v28: 'I have MADE (shith) the Lord GOD my refuge' - the act of setting God as his refuge (the char refuge, 282477); the making-God-his-shelter. Standalone (the making).
